components.note: Possibility/necessity (thm:p15-r47-threshold), static ranking transform with corrected complement orientation (annex 56-60 against source p.307 printed N(A^c)=2^-kappa(A)), and belief functions (def/thm focal, combination, pignistic) are kept separate with assumptions, a worked contrast and limitations, and the comparison table body 550-579.

components.gap: Complete argument not reconstructed for source sections 3.1, 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3. Missing from the LaTeX: (1) the Bayesian uniqueness principle (Lindley 1982) and the claim that de Finetti fair-bet coherence forces one distribution, the premise the section 4.1 critique targets (p.310); (2) the source's objection that Cox postulate (i) is natural only if the form of Bayes conditioning is presupposed, and Paris's replacement of condition (iii) by strict monotonicity in each argument (body 327-333 give only density/infinite assumptions and the self-duality point); (3) the AI-literature uptake (Horvitz-Heckerman-Langlotz, Cheeseman, Jaynes) that section 4.1 argues against appears only in \nocite; (4) the source's statement that general coherent lower probabilities satisfy only P(A u B) >= P(A)+P(B) for disjoint A,B, versus all-order super-additivity for belief functions (p.313), is not stated; (5) Hintikka's epistemic-logic framing (knowledge as true belief, ignorance as believing neither) and the KD45 axiom list with accessibility semantics (p.309) are not reconstructed, only delegated to a P08 sheet; (6) the Smith/Williams/Giles/Walley lineage of desirability and Shafer's theory as a reading of Dempster 1967 upper/lower probabilities and a revival of Bernoulli-Lambert probability (pp.311-312) are absent.

components.gap: Lottery, big-stepped, die, extraterrestrial life, log-uniform, simple-support testimony, reinforcement and likelihood examples are present with claim-type distinctions (body 118-147, 281-305, 342-413, 514-537). Missing: the source's claim that the maxmin rule on lower previsions solves the Ellsberg paradox whereas the LP(f-g) >= 0 rule satisfies Savage's sure-thing principle (p.313) is not presented with its assumptions; lemma body 467-475 separates the rules abstractly and annex 180-181 disclaims Ellsberg, but the actual Ellsberg/sure-thing contrast and its normative-versus-empirical status are not stated. The pignistic rule as a generalization of Laplace's insufficient-reason principle (p.312) is absent.

components.gap: Comparisons are made to P15 ranking theory (sec:p15-rationality-5-3), P15 imprecise-probability results, P14 evidence measures, P08 KD45 and KLM, and P18 argument strength (body 52, 169-182, 199-207, 272-274, 369-370, 449-465, 484, 544-548). The source explicitly links its de Finetti fair-price account to handbook chapter 4.1 (Hajek-Staffel, p.306), which exists as sec:p15-rationality-4-1 and is grouped with this unit in queue section 164.10, but the treatment never compares with or references it; the source's link to chapter 8.4 (Hill) on qualitative decision rules (p.308), present as sec:p17-rationality-8-4, is not compared either (body 106-114).

components.gap: Finite proofs are written in the annex (annex 4-210) for the threshold, big-stepped sufficiency, ranking, finite modal, ignorance, focal, combination, pignistic, price, Mobius and likelihood results, and GPL completeness and DPS 2008 least-information are marked as cited boundaries. Not accounted for: the source's characterization claim that probabilities satisfying conditional adjunction at 0.5 have the big-stepped form p1>...>pn with pi exceeding the sum of later masses (DFP 2004 / BDP 1999, p.308); thm:p15-r47-big-stepped proves sufficiency only and says it is not asserted to be the complete classification, without recording the source's converse as a cited claim with a proof target. Also: the claim that any convex set of probabilities can be represented by lower previsions on some family of gambles (p.312) is addressed only for closed convex sets on all bounded gambles (body 461-464) without engaging the source's unqualified statement; the Chateauneuf-Jaffray Mobius claim is proved but not attributed; Kyburg-Teng's logic of risky knowledge (pp.308, 310) is not named; the finite dependent-source set is fixed only as a \nocite list (body 581-600).
